paper.title_en: Thermodynamic performance and magnetocaloric response of a two-spin quantum working medium with DM and KSEA interactions
paper.abstract_en: The thermodynamic behavior and magnetocaloric response of Otto and Stirling quantum heat engines is investigated using a two-spin-1/2 XYZ working medium with antisymmetric Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM) and symmetric Kaplan-Shekhtman-Entin-Wohlman-Aharony (KSEA) interactions. The dependence of network, heat input, heat rejection, thermodynamic operation modes, and efficiency on the magnetic field ratio and interaction strengths is analyzed. It is shown that as the magnetic field ratio increases, the sign of the network changes from negative to positive, a trend that accompanies the transition from refrigerator-like to engine-like operation when the signs of the heat exchanges are also taken into account. The presence of DM interaction amplifies sensitivity to the magnetic field ratio, improving tunability. The Stirling cycles are demonstrated to have broader and more robust engine operation domains and higher maximum work output and efficiency, while the Otto cycles exhibit richer and more sensitive thermodynamic behavior with a wider dynamic range of network. Heat input patterns reveal non-monotonic dependence in the Otto cycles, influenced by interaction parameters, whereas the Stirling cycles display monotonic trends. Overall, the interplay of the magnetic field ratio and spin-orbit coupling is shown to actively control quantum engine performance and mode transitions. We demonstrate that the Stirling cycle becomes an engine at a lower magnetic field ratio than the Otto cycle, a finding with practical implications for low-field quantum thermal devices. We report opposite trends in heat absorption between the two cycles, directly linking cycle structure to the underlying energy-exchange mechanism. We show that DM interaction dramatically enhances magnetic field sensitivity, enabling precise work-output tuning-a feature absent in models with only KSEA or no spin-orbit coupling. These results fill a gap in the literature, where previous studies have typically examined only one cycle type or one interaction type at a time. Our unified framework reveals previously unreported interplay effects and control strategies.
